summary.headline: Sambhv Steel Tubes Q4 FY26 revenue rose 38% to INR685 crores and EBITDA 91% to INR92 crores, with record quarterly profit.
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue, EBITDA and PAT for Q4 FY26, with EBITDA per ton at INR9,500 excluding sponge iron sales, helped by raw-material lag and firm HR coil prices. For FY26, sales volume rose 37% to 3,96,000 tons, revenue 60% to INR2,413 crores and PAT more than doubled to INR143 crores. Capex was raised: the Kesda stainless steel Phase 1 (3,60,000 tpa) is on track for Q4 FY27, plus an additional INR200 crores of brownfield and power/DFT projects. Management guided Q1 FY27 EBITDA per ton to INR7,500-8,000 and FY27 average to INR7,000-8,000.

financial_highlights.metric: EBITDA per ton (Q4 FY26, excl. sponge iron)

financial_highlights.change: more than doubled; PAT margin 6% vs 3.8%

segments.name: Stainless steel (200/300 series CR coil)
segments.commentary: Capacity to rise from 58,000 to 1,16,000 tpa on debottlenecking, with consent to operate expected the week of the call. Management said 300 series is only about 10-20% of mix near term; FY26 SS sales were about 49,000 tons on 1,69,000 tons of total production including intermediates.

segments.name: Carbon steel (ERW pipes/tubes and GP/coated pipes)
segments.commentary: FY26 value-added volumes were 3,56,000 tons, up 51%. DFT line adds 1,50,000 tpa of ERW capacity for about INR50 crores, taking total ERW/tubes capacity to 0.5 million tpa by Q4 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 EBITDA per ton guided at INR7,500-8,000, described as achievable on current prices.
FY27 average EBITDA per ton guided at INR7,000-8,000, with volume growth of 10-15% over FY26.
Long-term EBITDA per ton of INR8,000-9,000 cited at about 60% utilisation by 2030; EBITDA margin band of 12% plus or minus 2%, PAT margin about 5% plus or minus 1%.
Working capital cycle expected at 17-25 days in FY27, rising to 25-30 days once stainless steel production is live in 2028.
Kesda Phase 1 (3,60,000 tpa SS) to commission in Q4 FY27; FY28 average utilisation not more than 40% in first year.
Peak long-term debt around INR800 crores plus INR200-300 crores working capital for announced capex; internal guardrails of long-term debt at most 1.5x net worth and 1.5x forward EBITDA.
Target of about 2 million tpa finished capacity by 2030 (10 lakh tons MS pipes/tubes, 3 lakh tons coated, 7 lakh tons SS).
capex_capacity: Kesda greenfield Phase 1: INR930 crores total, about INR300 crores spent so far, balance about INR630 crores, with about INR675 crores of term loan planned; 3,60,000 tpa stainless steel, commissioning Q4 FY27.

Additional INR200 crores of projects announced this quarter: 30 MW captive power plant at Sarora (INR150 crores, public hearing completed, expected to make Sarora power self-sufficient, power saving INR60-70 crores) and DFT line (1,50,000 tpa ERW for INR50 crores, Q4 FY27); up to INR150 crores debt, balance internal accrual.
Stainless steel CR debottlenecking: 58,000 to 1,16,000 tpa, consent to operate expected the week of the call.
Kesda 25 MW power plant to be self-sufficient for Phase 1 rolling mill; Kuthrel still imports some grid power.
Phase 2 and Phase 3 at Kesda not yet defined; management expects another INR300-400 crores of capex by FY28 once Phase 1 execution is clear.
Seamless pipe long product approved under PLI 1.2; project details and timeline to be announced after full approvals.
Utilisation targets: SS 60-65%, MS pipe/coil 65-70%, GP 80-90%, ERW 70-75% at maximum.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR930 crore capex is spent, how will it be funded, and what are the debt limits?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR300 crores spent, balance about INR630 crores with INR675 crores term loan planned for Kesda; the INR200 crores add-on is partly debt (max INR150 crores). Long-term debt capped at 1.5x net worth and 1.5x forward EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 EBITDA per ton so high, and what is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Procurement at lower raw-material prices in Q3 was consumed in Q4 while HR coil prices rose; Q1 FY27 guided at INR7,500-8,000 and FY27 average at INR7,000-8,000.

qa_highlights.question: Is the stainless steel production versus sales gap explained?
qa_highlights.answer: Production of 1,69,000 tons includes about 60,000 tons of slabs and 59,000 tons of HR coil that were captively consumed; saleable CR coil sales were about 49,000 tons. HR to CR recovery is about 98%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PLI 1.2 benefit and timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Thin-gauge CR coil PLI available till about 2030-31, capped at about INR200 crores or installed-capacity tonnage, at 13-15% of revenue depending on thickness and grade.

qa_highlights.question: What are Kesda's Phase 2 and 3 timelines and the 2030 aspiration?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 2 and 3 product mix not finalised; to be announced after Phase 1 utilisation is seen. 2030 target of 2 million tpa with 10-12% share in MS coil and pipes and SS flat products, and about 60% utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: How will the monsoon and Q1 demand look?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a below-normal El Nino monsoon forecast, which could lift demand; Q1 and Q4 typically strong for steel, Q2 and Q3 seasonally weaker.

risks_watch: Sustainability of INR7,000-8,000 EBITDA per ton once HR coil and raw material prices normalise, given Q4 benefited from inventory lag and price spike.
Kesda Phase 1 commissioning in Q4 FY27 and ramp-up; FY28 utilisation expected at no more than 40% in the first year.
Import pressure from China after October 10 non-BIS cutoff, and safeguard duty durability.
Working capital rising to 25-30 days as SS production starts in 2028.
Dependence on approvals for seamless pipe and Phase 2/3 product mix and capex quantum.
West Asia conflict effects on energy, zinc and alloy costs; management said plants ran 24x7 on PNG/LNG and domestic coal.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on Q4 and FY27 outlook, but evasive on Phase 2/3 capex quantum, product mix and seamless pipe timelines, deferring details until approvals and Phase 1 execution are in hand. Several answers were imprecise, notably on the INR100 crore investment classification and on the 40% inventory rise.

So our main purpose of IPO that we have brought is to go financial prudent and reduce our debt.

demand_pricing: Realisations Q4 FY26 (per ton): black MS pipe INR55,000-60,000; GP INR65,000-75,000; SS 200 series INR120,000-135,000; SS 300 series INR180,000-190,000.
Current-quarter indicative prices: black pipe INR57,000-60,000; GP about INR75,000; SS 200 about INR135,000; SS 300 about INR200,000-210,000.
Management said about 50-60% of realisation increases flow to EBITDA; rest goes via credit notes and customer discounts. Zinc, energy and other costs rose during the West Asia conflict.
HR coil moved from about INR45,000 (early December) to about INR56,000 per ton; management expects some reversal but believes HR coil will not fall sharply given safeguard duty and balanced supply.
Inventory up about 40% in line with revenue growth; management said stock valuation uses cost basis and about 60% of inventory is raw material.
Chinese SS import window: government set October 10 as final date for non-BIS imports; management expects some imports but sees no domestic pricing pressure.

growth.why: FY27 volume growth guided at 10-15% over FY26 (about 3.96 lakh t) and FY27 EBITDA/t of INR7,000-8,000, backed by Kesda Phase 1 (3.6 lakh tpa SS, Q4 FY27), SS CR debottlenecking to 1.16 lakh tpa and a 1.5 lakh tpa DFT ERW line, though Kesda's first-year utilisation is capped at 40% and the EBITDA/t guide is price-driven rather than volume-driven.
